https://bnn-news.com/split-in-polands-fa.text: Baltics Social Politics Money Interviews Opinions In Focus World Leisure Advertising Baltics Social Politics Money Interviews Opinions In Focus World Leisure Advertising Home Politics Politics World Split in Poland’s far-right party ranks – joy without guarantee of victory for centrists BNN August 10, 2026 Facebook Twitter Photo: Mateusz Włodarczyk/MRPiPS/Flickr The split in the right-wing conservative Law and Justice (PiS) party is a development that the centrist and pro-European government of Donald Tusk has welcomed, but it is unclear whether it will improve the current prime minister’s chances in the election, writes Politico. In the “Politico” “Poll of Polls” survey, Tusk’s Civic Coalition party is in the lead, with 32% of voters’ support, while PiS is supported by 21% of Polish voters. True, the survey results do not show the full picture of the electoral dynamics. All right-wing parties together could form a majority, but only if they can agree on a coalition after the elections scheduled for next year. Meanwhile, three of Tusk’s four coalition partners could not cross the 5% barrier needed to enter parliament. Renata Mieńkowska-Norkiene, a political scientist at the University of Warsaw, said Tusk’s chances of winning the election were far from clear. At the same time, the departure of former Polish Prime Minister Mateusz Morawiecki from PiS has complicated the balance of power on the right. The reins of power were in PiS’s hands from 2015 to 2023, but in July Morawiecki left the party, taking 40 other MPs with him. The differences between Morawiecki and PiS founder and leader Jarosław Kaczyński had taken on acrimonious tones. Morawiecki has criticized his own government’s decisions on pandemic-time restrictions and efforts to tighten abortion laws. The abortion issue in particular has sparked widespread protests, and support for the party has plummeted. Morawiecki said in a popular YouTube show in Poland, Rymanowski Live, that he himself is against abortion, but believes that tightening the law would lead to a ratings disaster, and he was unfortunately right. Now the former prime minister is trying to build a more moderate, center-right party focused on promoting economic growth. He said that Poland today does not need to descend to ideological disputes. At the same time, Morawiecki ruled out the possibility of forming a coalition with Tusk. Kaczyński responded by questioning both Morawiecki’s loyalty and common sense. He said that Morawiecki’s latest statements clearly show that the enemy is not Tusk, but Kaczyński and PiS, and the former prime minister is not quite in his right mind. On the 7th of August, Kaczyński added insult to injury by denouncing on the X attacks based on lies, manipulation and innuendo, carried out by people who once pretended to want to be part of PiS, but have now split from the party. Meanwhile, Tusk said he was happy to watch what was happening. Although Tusk’s party and PiS have alternated in power for more than two decades, the current political landscape is more complex. On the far right, two parties are fighting for voter support – the libertarian Confederation (14% support) and the anti-Semitic extremist Confederation of the Polish Crown (11%). Both parties are fighting among themselves, and also with PiS. Political experts have warned that Tusk should not count on the fact that the split within PiS will benefit him. Mjenkowski-Norkiene said that Kaczyński’s and Morawiecki’s parties could attract a wider range of voters separately than if they were a single party, while Tusk’s chances are based on the electoral performance of the coalition’s weaker parties. She added that Morawiecki’s party could attract the most conservative voters of these parties. Anna Siewierska-Chmaj, a political scientist at the University of Rzeszów, said that Tusk’s coalition should not rely solely on its opponents devouring themselves, and should instead spend the summer holidays changing its political message. Many voters are fed up with the government’s lack of results (and it doesn’t matter that this is partly due to the vetoes of many laws by Polish President Karol Nawrocki, who supports PiS). The scientist said that the previous “us against PiS” strategy will no longer work. Read also: Poland to ask US to extradite former Justice Minister Follow us on Facebook and X ! https://komonews.com/news/nation-world/m.text: HUNGARY (WKRC) - A 24-year-old man was arrested after authorities said he stole a small plane from an airport in Hungary, prompting a military response before the aircraft made an emergency landing in a sunflower field. Police said they received a report Aug. 29 that a small aircraft had made an emergency landing near Gerjen in Tolna County. Investigators determined the man had taken a Cessna 172 from an airport in Kalocsa and headed toward Paks, a nuclear power plant, according to Hungarian authorities. The Hungarian Defense Forces said military radar detected the unauthorized aircraft and a pair of Gripen fighter jets was scrambled in response. A few minutes later, the Cessna made an emergency landing near Gerjen. The fighter jets located the damaged aircraft and remained over the area until a rescue helicopter and ground crews arrived, according to the defense forces. No injuries were reported. Authorities said the man left the plane and began walking along a nearby road in what police described as a confused state. A passing motorist stopped to help him, but police said the man got into the vehicle and attempted to drive away. He was stopped before he could leave. Officers arrested the 24-year-old nearby within minutes. Police said preliminary information indicated the man was intoxicated. Investigators are also trying to determine whether he was under the influence of another substance.

https://www.manchestereveningnews.co.uk/.text: It started with a flood of complaints. Then it grew into a major nationwide investigation and the biggest case Salford Trading Standards has ever taken on. When the country was in lockdown, due to Covid, Rael Flavius Nicola saw an opportunity. Restrictions in 2020 linked to the pandemic meant it was difficult for businesses and the public to buy commercial vehicles. Many people were desperate for vans during the pandemic as they tried to work as couriers after losing their jobs. Nicola exploited that need. For the next four years, through Facebook he sold second hand vans. On his website for the business he pledged to sell quality used cars and vans. The truth was somewhat different. A trading standards investigation which began in late 2020 revealed a major fraud. The scam was so extensive Salford council officers got funding support from National Trading Standards so that two local officers could concentrate solely on the investigation. They also found that Mr Nicola created fake service history books, complete with counterfeit garage stamps, to give buyers the impression that vehicles had been properly maintained, raising serious concerns about the safety and condition of vehicles being sold to consumers. In addition, Mr Nicola instructed an accomplice to wind back vehicle odometers — known as “clocking” — to make vehicles appear less used and therefore more valuable and attempted to conceal the true condition of vehicles by painting over rust and corrosion and preventing buyers from identifying serious faults before purchase. Mileage on four of the vehicles that were scrutinised in the investigation had been reduced by, 49,787 miles; 126,923; 164,348; and astonishingly one by 272,499 miles. The vans were stored at Orchard Sawmills, Langley Road South, Salford. Mr Nicola also falsely told customers that they were insured to drive vehicles away at the point of sale, despite no such insurance being in place. Victims were further misled into believing their vehicles came with a six-month warranty. When they later attempted to make claims, it became clear that the warranties were entirely fictitious. During the investigation, Trading Standards officers discovered that Mr Nicola had used 15 different aliases when registering vehicles with the DVLA and when dealing with customers. This significantly complicated efforts to trace his activities and required extensive management of digital evidence to support the case.. One of his aliases was Robbinu Nicola - meaning Robbing you Nicola in Romanian. At Manchester Crown Court Mr Nicola of Somerset Road, Eccles , Salford, received an 18 month sentence, suspended for 20 months, 250 hours unpaid work and was ordered to pay £23,600 compensation to seven victims after being convicted of nine offences of fraud, including fraud by false representation and carrying on a business for a fraudulent purpose. In sentencing, the court took into account the sustained and deliberate nature of the offending, the deception of multiple victims alongside the financial losses incurred and the intimidation used to suppress complaints. Councillor Barbara Bentham, Salford City Council's lead member for Neighbourhoods, Environment and Community, said: "This case highlights the serious harm that fraudulent traders can cause to hardworking residents and local businesses. These actions were deliberate, sustained and calculated to exploit members of the public. “I would like to thank National Trading Standards for its financial support to assist the investigation and Salford Trading Standards for their thorough investigation and commitment to protecting consumers. We will continue to take robust action against people who seek to exploit people in our communities, and we hope today’s sentencing provides reassurance that such conduct will not be tolerated.” Lord Michael Bichard, Chair of National Trading Standards, said: "This was a calculated deception that cost victims significant sums of money and put them in danger by leading them to believe they were driving vehicles that were roadworthy, insured and legally compliant. "Fraudulent traders like this also undermine honest vehicle dealers who work hard to earn the trust of their customers and compete fairly. “The sentence demonstrates that those who seek to profit through dishonesty can expect to be investigated and held to account.” Salford Trading Standards officer Valmai Jones said: "The vans were being sold across the UK. When we were really drilling in and investigating him it was over a period (in 2020) of two and half months in which he sold vans. But we were able to seize documentation over a period of two years. "The invoices of people he had sold vehicles to had people's addresses on so we contacted them all. There were 84 in total over two years. That's just the invoices we found. Some of the complainants never got an invoice. We had complainants from as far away as the Isle of Wight, Belfast, Peterborough, Gravesend, and Wales. "They were coming from all over because he was selling vans in the deepest, darkest period of Covid. In September 2020 you could not get a van for love or money. A lot of people had been made redundant from their work which meant taking jobs as delivery drivers as shops were closed and people went online for goods. These were people that were in dire straits - not all of them, but a significant amount of them. It was very calculated in that sense. "It is very difficult to quantify how much money he made as mostly he took cash. We were able to work out from the documentation seized that the sale price of the 84 vehicles was £258,000. He will have to paid something for the vehicles but his turnover for 2019 and 2020 was a quarter of million pounds." Initially trading standards officers thought they were dealing with someone selling vans privately. Then there was a huge spike in complaints in mid 2020. "It was not a traditional car lot. It was behind locked gates. There were vans but no signs they were for sale. I started to look every single day at what he was advertising on Facebook. "I took screen shots of the vehicles, the descriptions. They would have the registration numbers on so we could look at the MOTs. It would say there was an MOT for 12 months, but when we checked there was no MOT. "Between the end of September and beginning of December 2020. I checked every day what he was selling. In that time he had 24 vehicles for sale and the asking price for them all was £160,000 - those sales were in a really concentrated part of 2020. "Mercedes Sprinters were his bread and butter. They were the preferred vehicle as they are reliable an go for years." The seizure of phones when warrants were carried out on Mr Nicola's home and business premises revealed evidence of vehicles being clocked. "We found text messages from him to someone else where he is stating a registration number and a mileage next to it," said Valmai. But when officers put the registration into the MOT history online they could see that the mileage at the previous MOT was already much higher than the one he was requesting for it. "When people complained about the mileage having checked previous MOTs he would tell them, don't worry it has got a new engine, and people were taken in by that. The fact is you can't justify putting mileage back by saying there is a new engine. The mileage is not just a reflection of the miles travelled and the engine, it is everything, the chassis, and all other parts." She added: "One of the witnesses in the case described driving on the motorway and the bonnet flying up because the catch was broken. He had to swerve into the hard shoulder. When he rang Rael Flavius Nicola about that and various other things like it was not MOT''d, he was told 'don't ring me again or I am going to come and burn your house down'. "Bearing in mind he knows the addresses of all these people (who have complained) people were scared. We wrote to all 84 of the people whose invoices we found to ask them if there was a problem. Some may have been blissfully unaware that their vehilce had been clocked. "We were trying to get people to be witnesses and in the end we could only get seven because people were scared to be a witness, which I totally understand. These people were very brave to come forward. "He pleaded guilty at the first opportunity because we had him hog-tied. He could not deny it. It was bigger than anything we have ever done in Salford before. "One of the aliases he used beggars belief. In text messages customers sometimes asked him what his name was. He replied Robbinu Nicola (as in ‘robbing you’) this was mentioned in court. This showed – to me anyway – how cocky and arrogant he was. "I’m not aware of any consumers that were actually taken in by this alias…only that he called himself that when potential customers contacted him about vans for sale. The seven witnesses we had did not know him as that name. "He referred to himself as Robbinu in text messages when people were enquiring about buying from him or when he was trying to buy stock himself. It was mentioned in his defence in court that when he put Robbinu – he had meant to put Robin Hood." "The compensation awarded goes to the seven brave witnesses that came forwards and gave a statement. They would have had to give evidence in court if it had come to that – luckily it didn’t. "Obviously – it’s a low figure compared to the money he made but we can only ask for compensation for the witnesses in the case. He was spared having to pay any costs, which were substantial, due to apparently having no money." Consumers concerned about rogue traders can report issues to Trading Standards via the Citizens Advice Consumer Helpline on 0808 223 1133. Salford trading standards officers say buyers have to be particularly wary of traders who only operate online, use multiple names, or refuse to provide a fixed business address. Consumers should always be suspicious of deals that appear too good to be true and Independently verify that a vehicle is taxed, has an MOT certificate and insured, rather than relying on verbal assurances. They should view the vehicle in good lighting and look for signs of concealed damage, such as freshly painted areas covering rust or corrosion. They should check mileage history carefully and be alert to signs of odometer tampering. They should request and verify genuine service history, contacting garages directly if necessary and never feel pressured into completing a sale quickly. Consumers need to be aware that fraudulent traders may attempt to intimidate or reassure buyers with false claims about insurance, documentation, or legal protection. If a seller becomes evasive, aggressive, or discourages independent checks, buyers should walk away immediately." Anyone who believes they have been a victim of vehicle fraud should alert Trading Standards via the Citizens Advice Consumer Service, so that patterns of offending can be identified and investigated. Trading Standards stress that taking time to carry out checks before buying can prevent significant financial loss and disruption, particularly where vehicles are needed for work or business purposes.
